newsitem.title: USA: Pegasus sees 15 pct rise in '97 output.
newsitem.headline: Pegasus sees 15 pct rise in '97 output.

text.p: Pegasus Gold Inc said it expects 1997 gold production to rise 15 percent from 1996 to 570,000 ounces.

The company attributed the anticipated rise to a new processing facility at Mt. Todd reaching commercial production in the second quarter and Florida Canyon continuing to operate two crushers through 1997.
Pegasus Gold also said it plans about $50 million in capital expenditures in 1997.
Total cash costs are expected to be $300 per ounce for the year, the company said.
The company anticipates $18.3 million in 1997 spending for Mt Todd to complete the commissioning of the processing facility and for maintenance.
At Zortman, $11.8 million will be spent for water quality compliance, reclamation and a feasibility study that is expected to be finished in July.
Pegasus Gold said it will not begin construction on the Zortman extension project until 1998 due to weak prices.
Weak prices and limited success of exploration drilling also have prompted Pegasus to delay the start of construction of the new milling and heap leach facility to 1998.

"While the company's current development program will delay some projects, it is still the company's goal to achieve a million ounces of gold production by the year 2000. To realize this goal, the company is maintaining an active business development program to search for opportunities in addition to its exploration," said chief executive officer Werner Nennecker.
By 1999, gold production is expected to be nearly 38 percent higher than 1996 levels, the company said.
Pegasus Gold also said it planned an $11 million exploration program for 1997 exclusive of its prefunded program at Intermin.
Key operations at Mt. Todd, Florida Canyon, and Montana Tunnels are expected to report total cash costs in 1997 of $300, $300, and $270 per ounce, respectively.
The company also said it has adopted the Gold Institute Standard for reporting production costs. As a result, royalties are now included in cash costs.
